questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding. Wear it even on warm days.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers. Bright colors with reflective materials help other road users see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps the group close while giving each rider a safe distance from others.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Limit your riding time each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit your riding time each day.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest on long trips, even if you do not feel tired. Do not ride more than six hours a day. Wind, cold, and rain can make you tired faster, so dress to protect yourself from weather.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should generally be:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close while giving each one enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to allow the wind to catch the fabric.
Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to prevent you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind. They should also be loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are never very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, have side effects that can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will properly yield.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. When released, the throttle should:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your throttle and clutch. The throttle should snap back when released, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can reduce your riding ability. You can be convicted of impaired riding even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign has white background with red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcycle riders is:
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best foot protection while riding. Boots should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: The human body removes alcohol at a rate of:
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour on average. This varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, your main concern should be the helmet's:
questions.explanation: When choosing a helmet, protection is the most important factor.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is changing to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to see everything around you. Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best protection. They should be high and strong enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your top priority when buying a helmet. Choose one that fits well, fastens securely, and has a DOT safety rating.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, what should you do?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to shift into higher gears.

questions.question: Which item is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible when riding.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel under 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned when holding the handlebars?
questions.explanation: Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces fatigue and lets you control the bike without stretching.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when it first rains. Rainwater mixes with oil left by cars on the road. Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars to get better grip.

questions.question: What should you know about motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: The mirrors provide a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should not be used, except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a protective jacket?

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket made of leather or strong synthetic material. It should cover your arms completely, fit snugly, and allow you to move freely. Built-in body armor provides the best protection.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you to use their headlights.
Reduce your speed to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards when visibility is low. Also increase your following distance and be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: How should your riding speed change at night?

options.text: Ride as fast as you would during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: At night, especially on unfamiliar roads, ride more slowly than during the day. Riding slowly gives you more time to avoid hazards when you cannot see as well.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist stop quickly?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Watch the road ahead to help you avoid needing to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always do a safety check of your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should happen if two vehicles arrive at the same time?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
Speed up to increase distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: If safe, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.
